description: Flat 8 m square of exposed-aggregate pebble-wash paving in cast panels with divider strips -- one quad, one seamless PBR texture set, tiling in both axes.

image.prompt:
A SEAMLESSLY TILING TOP-DOWN GROUND TEXTURE. This is a flat material swatch, not a photograph of a scene or of an object. The camera looks straight down at the ground from directly overhead, perfectly orthographic, with no perspective, no horizon, no vanishing point and no tilt.

The surface: Flat square of exposed aggregate pebble wash paving seen as a single unbroken surface, small rounded river pebbles set densely flush into cement, divided into equal square panels by thin straight metal divider strips running both ways, edge to edge pebble surface only, no kerb and no border Materials: Seamlessly tiling small rounded river pebbles in warm cream, tan, grey and rust brown set flush in pale grey cement with the tops exposed and rubbed smooth, thin tarnished brass divider strips between panels, tonal drift panel to panel, dark grime and moss collected in the cement between pebbles along the shaded runs, a few pebbles lost leaving small pits, damp staining and pale efflorescence near the strips; the pebble scatter and the divider grid must both wrap on all four edges with no pebble cluster repeating across a seam.

Scale: the square shown covers exactly 8 by 8 metres of real ground, so every stone, block, slab, joint, marking, rut and tuft in it is drawn at its true size relative to that. Do not zoom in on a detail and do not pull back to show a wider scene.

Tiling: the texture must repeat seamlessly on all four edges. What runs off the left edge continues onto the right edge, and what runs off the top continues onto the bottom, exactly. No feature may be cut in half at an edge without its other half appearing at the opposite edge. Laid out four by four this must read as one continuous surface with no visible grid, no repeated landmark feature and no seam.

Framing: the surface fills the entire frame edge to edge and corner to corner. There is no border, no frame, no margin, no backdrop, no background, no matte and no empty space of any kind. The ground continues past every edge of the image.

Nothing stands on it and nothing bounds it: no kerb, no wall, no step, no gutter, no drain, no manhole cover, no grass verge, no plants, no people, no vehicles, no furniture, no objects, no litter, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows.

Lighting: flat, even, shadowless overhead illumination, like a lightbox. The image is the surface's true albedo. No sun, no cast shadows, no directional highlights, no specular blowout, no vignette, no gradient across the frame, no baked ambient occlusion in the corners and crevices, no light falloff towards the edges -- an uneven frame cannot tile, because its bright side would meet its dark side at every seam.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, realistic material, real surface wear and staining. Not stylised, not cartoon, not a 3D render preview, not a tiled collage of separate photographs, not a pattern illustration.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

name: Pebble-Wash Terrazzo Paving Tile
nameTh: พื้นหินล้าง
notes: One flat quad, 8 x 8 m, lying in the ground plane at y=0 -- two triangles, one geometry, one draw call, one PBR material, and nothing else. The entire surface reads out of the texture; every pebble is normal and AO relief, not geometry. This is a member of the kit's ground-surface tile set: every tile in that set is 8 x 8 m, sits at y=0, uses pivot base-center and snaps on the kit's 8 m grid, so it butts flush against any other ground tile and against the asphalt road tiles, and the raised Concrete Sidewalk Strip (2.0 m wide, 0.15 m tall) sits alongside as a separate object. Pebble wash is one of the most recognisably Thai outdoor surfaces and has no close equivalent elsewhere in the kit: it covers temple walkways, condo and hotel entrance courts, school corridors, park paths and the aprons of civic buildings, and its warm speckle is what makes a paved area read as Thailand rather than as generic concrete. It is deliberately distinct from the Cobblestone Paving Tile, which is chunky proud stone setts with open sandy joints; this is small pebbles set FLUSH in a cement matrix, cast in panels, with thin divider strips and no joint relief to speak of. The divider strips form a SQUARE panel grid whose pitch must divide 8 m evenly and wrap on all four edges, which makes the tile fully FOUR-way rotationally symmetric -- it drops in at any of four orientations. The first thing to check on the generated texture is that no distinctive pebble cluster repeats across a seam, because a dense small-scale scatter shows a bad wrap far more readily than a coarse pattern does. Budget overridden explicitly to 2 triangles / 1 draw call / 1 material / 1 unique geometry instead of the hero2x its 8 m footprint would derive: footprint drives the class, but there is no geometry here to spend a class budget on. No destruction groups: a ground tile is static level geometry, not a breakable.
